```{r, echo = FALSE, message=FALSE}
# plotly.js from the CDN, so the site's pages don't each copy it
options(plotly.core.plotlyjs = "cdn")
```
### Introduction

In order to complete the examples below, you'll require installing additional packages (`install.packages("packageName")`):
- [sf](https://github.com/r-spatial/sf)
- [geojsonsf](https://github.com/SymbolixAU/geojsonsf)

The examples below use the library [simple features](https://r-spatial.github.io/sf/) to read in the shape files before plotting the features with Plotly. plotly.core doesn't draw `sf` objects directly, so the examples convert them to coordinates or GeoJSON first.

### Map Tiles

Tile-based maps (`add_choroplethmap()`, `add_scattermap()`, ...) use MapLibre and need no access token. See the [Map Layers](https://plotly.com/r/mapbox-layers/) documentation for more information.

### Basic sf

The polygon coordinates can be drawn as filled scatter paths, with `NA` separating the rings:

```{r}
library(plotly.core)
library(sf)

nc <- sf::st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"), quiet = TRUE)

coords <- as.data.frame(sf::st_coordinates(nc))
rings <- split(coords, list(coords$L1, coords$L2, coords$L3), drop = TRUE)
x <- unlist(lapply(rings, function(r) c(r$X, NA)), use.names = FALSE)
y <- unlist(lapply(rings, function(r) c(r$Y, NA)), use.names = FALSE)

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(
    x = x,
    y = y,
    mode = "lines",
    fill = "toself",
    line = go_scatter_line(width = 1)
  ) |>
  update_yaxes(scaleanchor = "x")

fig
```

You can also draw the features on a geo map with `add_choropleth()`, passing them as GeoJSON:

```{r}
library(plotly.core)
library(sf)

nc <- sf::st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"), quiet = TRUE)
nc_geojson <- jsonlite::fromJSON(
  geojsonsf::sf_geojson(nc),
  simplifyVector = FALSE
)

fig <- nc |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_choropleth(
    geojson = nc_geojson,
    locations = ~NAME,
    featureidkey = "properties.NAME",
    z = ~AREA,
    colorscale = "Viridis"
  ) |>
  update_geos(fitbounds = "locations", visible = FALSE)

fig
```

Or on a tile map with `add_choroplethmap()`:

```{r}
library(plotly.core)
library(sf)

nc <- sf::st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"), quiet = TRUE)
nc_geojson <- jsonlite::fromJSON(
  geojsonsf::sf_geojson(nc),
  simplifyVector = FALSE
)

fig <- nc |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_choroplethmap(
    geojson = nc_geojson,
    locations = ~NAME,
    featureidkey = "properties.NAME",
    z = seq_len(nrow(nc)),
    colorscale = "Turbo",
    showscale = FALSE,
    marker = go_choroplethmap_marker(opacity = 0.6),
    text = ~NAME,
    hoverinfo = "text"
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    map = go_map(
      style = "carto-positron",
      zoom = 6,
      center = go_map_center(lon = -79.5, lat = 35.5)
    )
  )

fig
```
### Reference

See `go_choropleth()` and `go_choroplethmap()` for more information and chart attribute options! If you would like to read more on visualizing geo-spatial data with sf and plotly click [here](https://blog.cpsievert.me/2018/03/30/visualizing-geo-spatial-data-with-sf-and-plotly/).
